title: 222. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Solving Equations with Piecewise Conditions
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Solving absolute value equations by piecewise cases
questions.learningObjective: Solve an absolute value equation by considering both cases of the expression inside the absolute value.
questions.question: Solve \(|x-3|=5\).
questions.explanation: The equation \(|x-3|=5\) means \(x-3=5\) or \(x-3=-5\). Solving gives \(x=8\) or \(x=-2\). Therefore the solutions are \(x=-2\) or \(x=8\).
questions.hint: Split the absolute value equation into two linear equations, one for each possible sign.

questions.concept: Solving absolute value equations by piecewise cases
questions.learningObjective: Solve an absolute value equation with a linear expression by checking both cases.
questions.question: Solve \(|2x+1|=7\).
questions.hint: Solve the two linear equations obtained by removing the absolute value with a positive and negative sign.

questions.concept: Solving absolute value equations after isolating the absolute value
questions.learningObjective: Solve an absolute value equation by first isolating the absolute value expression and then using cases.
questions.question: Solve \(|x-2|+3=7\).
questions.explanation: Subtract \(3\) from both sides: \(|x-2|=4\). Then \(x-2=4\) or \(x-2=-4\). These give \(x=6\) or \(x=-2\). Therefore the solutions are \(x=-2\) or \(x=6\).
questions.hint: First isolate the absolute value expression, then split it into two cases.

questions.concept: Solving absolute value equations with a nonnegative condition
questions.learningObjective: Solve \(|x+1|=2x-3\) and reject any solution that violates the condition \(2x-3\ge0\).
questions.question: Solve \(|x+1|=2x-3\).
questions.explanation: Since the left side is an absolute value, the right side must satisfy \(2x-3\ge0\), so \(x\ge\frac{3}{2}\). Now solve the cases. If \(x+1=2x-3\), then \(x=4\), which satisfies \(x\ge\frac{3}{2}\). If \(x+1=-(2x-3)\), then \(x+1=-2x+3\), so \(3x=2\), giving \(x=\frac{2}{3}\). But \(\frac{2}{3}<\frac{3}{2}\), so it is rejected. Therefore the only solution is \(x=4\).
questions.hint: Require the right side to be nonnegative before solving the two cases.

questions.concept: Solving absolute value equations with two valid cases
questions.learningObjective: Solve \(|2x-5|=x+1\) and verify both possible solutions against the condition \(x+1\ge0\).
questions.question: Solve \(|2x-5|=x+1\).
questions.explanation: The right side equals an absolute value, so \(x+1\ge0\), meaning \(x\ge-1\). If \(2x-5=x+1\), then \(x=6\), which satisfies \(x\ge-1\). If \(2x-5=-(x+1)\), then \(2x-5=-x-1\), so \(3x=4\), giving \(x=\frac{4}{3}\), which also satisfies \(x\ge-1\). Therefore the solutions are \(x=\frac{4}{3}\) or \(x=6\).
questions.hint: Check the condition \(x+1\ge0\), then solve both linear cases.

questions.concept: Solving equations with absolute values on both sides
questions.learningObjective: Solve \(|x-4|=|2x+1|\) by equating the inside expressions or their opposites.
questions.question: Solve \(|x-4|=|2x+1|\).
questions.explanation: For two absolute values to be equal, the inside expressions are equal or opposite. If \(x-4=2x+1\), then \(-5=x\), so \(x=-5\). If \(x-4=-(2x+1)\), then \(x-4=-2x-1\), so \(3x=3\), giving \(x=1\). Therefore the solutions are \(x=-5\) or \(x=1\).
questions.hint: Set the two inside expressions equal, and also set one equal to the negative of the other.

questions.concept: Solving equations defined by piecewise functions
questions.learningObjective: Solve \(f(x)=4\) for a piecewise-defined function by testing each piece and its condition.
questions.question:
Let
\[
f(x)=
\begin{cases}
x+2, & x<0\\
x^2, & x\ge0
\end{cases}
\]
Solve \(f(x)=4\).
questions.explanation: On the piece \(x<0\), solve \(x+2=4\), giving \(x=2\). But \(2<0\) is false, so this solution is rejected. On the piece \(x\ge0\), solve \(x^2=4\), giving \(x=2\) or \(x=-2\). Since only \(x=2\) satisfies \(x\ge0\), the solution is \(x=2\).
questions.hint: Solve the equation on each piece separately, then keep only solutions that satisfy that piece's condition.

questions.concept: Solving equations defined by piecewise functions
questions.learningObjective: Solve a piecewise-defined equation and reject solutions that do not satisfy the active condition.
questions.question:
Let
\[
f(x)=
\begin{cases}
2x-1, & x\le1\\
x^2, & x>1
\end{cases}
\]
Solve \(f(x)=3\).
questions.explanation: On the piece \(x\le1\), solve \(2x-1=3\), giving \(x=2\). But \(2\le1\) is false, so this solution is rejected. On the piece \(x>1\), solve \(x^2=3\), giving \(x=\sqrt{3}\) or \(x=-\sqrt{3}\). Since only \(x=\sqrt{3}\) satisfies \(x>1\), the solution is \(x=\sqrt{3}\).
questions.hint: For each piece, solve the equation and check the solution against that piece's condition.

questions.concept: Solving equations defined by piecewise functions with absolute value
questions.learningObjective: Solve a piecewise-defined equation involving an absolute value and verify each solution against its condition.
questions.question:
Let
\[
f(x)=
\begin{cases}
|x-1|, & x<2\\
3x-6, & x\ge2
\end{cases}
\]
Solve \(f(x)=2\).
questions.explanation: On the piece \(x<2\), solve \(|x-1|=2\). This gives \(x-1=2\) or \(x-1=-2\), so \(x=3\) or \(x=-1\). Only \(x=-1\) satisfies \(x<2\). On the piece \(x\ge2\), solve \(3x-6=2\), giving \(3x=8\), so \(x=\frac{8}{3}\). Since \(\frac{8}{3}\ge2\), this solution is valid. Therefore the solutions are \(x=-1\) or \(x=\frac{8}{3}\).
questions.hint: Solve each piece separately, then keep only the values that satisfy the corresponding condition.

questions.concept: Solving equations with two absolute values by interval cases
questions.learningObjective: Solve \(|x-3|+|x+1|=6\) by dividing the number line into intervals and checking each case.
questions.question: Solve \(|x-3|+|x+1|=6\).
questions.explanation: The critical values are \(x=-1\) and \(x=3\). Test the three intervals. If \(x<-1\), then \(|x-3|=-(x-3)\) and \(|x+1|=-(x+1)\), so \(-(x-3)-(x+1)=6\). This simplifies to \(-2x+2=6\), giving \(x=-2\), which satisfies \(x<-1\). If \(-1\le x<3\), the left side simplifies to \(4\), which is not \(6\). If \(x\ge3\), then \((x-3)+(x+1)=6\), giving \(2x-2=6\), so \(x=4\), which satisfies \(x\ge3\). Therefore the solutions are \(x=-2\) or \(x=4\).
questions.hint: Use the critical values where each absolute value expression changes sign, then solve the equation on each interval.
